chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Umar ibn Abi Ziyad, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

'Verily, God — Mighty and Majestic — created the creatures and created their sustenance along with them, permissible and wholesome. So whoever takes anything from it through forbidden means, a corresponding amount is deducted from that permissible sustenance.'

key_terms.أَرْزَاق: rizq (provisions/sustenance) — the divinely allocated share of material provision that God has destined for each creature
key_terms.حَلَالًا طَيِّباً: halal and tayyib — permissible and wholesome; a Quranic pairing (cf. 2:168, 5:88) emphasizing both legal permissibility and intrinsic goodness
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: 'Azza wa Jalla — Mighty and Majestic; a standard honorific for God in hadith literature
key_terms.قُصَّ: was cut/deducted — from the root q-s-s, meaning to trim or reduce; indicates a divine subtraction from one's allotted halal provision

ai.seo_question: Does earning haram income reduce a Muslim's halal sustenance according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that God created every person's sustenance (rizq) as inherently halal and pure from the moment of creation — it exists as a divine allocation. When a person acquires sustenance through haram means, they do not gain extra provision; rather, they lose an equivalent portion from their rightful halal sustenance, suffering a net loss both spiritually and practically. This hadith addresses a common misunderstanding — that haram income 'supplements' one's livelihood — and clarifies that the divine economy of provision operates on principles of moral accountability.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Al Sandy, from Ja’far Bin Bashir, from Umar Bin Abu Ziyad, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Created the creatures and Created their sustenances along with them, Permissible, good. So the one who attains anything from it by a Prohibited means, there would be a reduction from that Permissible (sustenance)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn al-Sindiy from Ja’far ibn Bashir from ‘Umar ibn abu Ziyad from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has created the creatures and with them He has created their sustenance of the lawful and beautiful kind. If anyone achieves a certain amount of unlawful sustenance it, then is deducted from his lawful sustenance.’”
